exam.title: Cisco Certified Support Technician Networking
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite. Build packet-delivery reasoning across models, performance, applications/protocols, IPv4/IPv6 addressing and subnet formats, endpoint/media selection, switching/routing/services, safe Cisco and operating-system inspection, evidence-led troubleshooting/ticketing, and foundational network/wireless security using Packet Tracer or equipment you are authorized to operate.

review.notes: All six public topic groups and every first-party exam-aligned course objective are mapped through packet delivery, IPv4/IPv6, endpoints/media, switching/routing/services, evidence-led diagnosis/ticketing and foundational security. Three scenarios, eight authorized labs and 36 checks are included. No stable public domain weights were found, so none are invented. Eight links are reachable and two O'Reilly pages are automation-blocked; none are missing or broken.

findings.title: General Continuing Education guidance excludes CCST
Training overview is not the detailed exam blueprint
TCP443 is not every HTTPS transport
Subtracting two addresses is not universal
An assigned IPv6 address does not prove a default router
Capture exclusion cannot be undone by display filtering
A Boolean field can exist when its value is false
A local outgoing bad checksum can precede hardware completion
IPv4 header integrity does not cover payload
Remote IP and local next-hop MAC serve different scopes
A DNS negative response differs from no observed response
